1. The "2026-Crop Loan Waiver Scheme" shall apply only to the crop loans disbursed by the following Cooperative Societies by obtaining cash credit from Central Cooperative Banks:-

(1) Primary Agricultural Cooperative Credit Societies, Large Area Multi-Purpose Cooperative Societies, Cultivators Cooperative Societies, Rural Cooperative Credit Societies, Farmers Service Cooperative Societies, and Urban Cooperative Credit Societies.

(Il) Societies that were originally Primary Agricultural Cooperative Credit Societies and subsequently converted into Urban Cooperative Credit Societies.

(a) Short-term crop loan

(b) Short-term crop loan issued against the pledge of jewel (Jewel loan for agricultural purposes)

(c) Joint Liability Group crop loan

3. This scheme shall apply only to those who fall under the classification of marginal / small / other farmers as per the Land Ownership Register / 10(1) Chitta / Adangal / Society Loan Registers as on the date of loan sanction. It shall not apply to the classification based on the actual cultivated area for which the loan was obtained. Marginal farmers are those with landholding up to 2.5 acres. Small farmers are those with landholding above 2.5 acres and up to 5 acres. Other farmers are those with landholding above 5 acres.

4. This scheme shall not apply to cases subjected to legal actions such as inquiry, inspection, surcharge proceedings, financial irregularities, and criminal proceedings initiated under Sections 81, 82, and 87 of the Tamil Nadu Cooperative Societies Act, 1983. In such cases, the benefits of this scheme shall be extended to the farmers based on the final outcome of the aforementioned legal actions.

5. This scheme shall not apply to loans issued on the basis of fake documents, fabricated documents, or unreliable documents, as well as benami loans.

Method of Calculation

6. The waiver amount received from the Government (partial / full amount) shall be adjusted against the outstanding loan, interest and principal amount.

7. The loan exposure of an eligible farmer shall be reduced in proportion to the waiver amount received from the Government. The exposure on the outstanding loan of the eligible farmer shall continue to remain.

8. If any subsidy has been received from the Government for crop loans under Government schemes, only the remaining amount, excluding the received subsidy, shall be waived.

9. The concerned credit societies shall bear the penal interest and other expenses related to crop loans eligible for the waiver, subject to the approval of the Administrator / Administrative Committee (Board-approved policy).

6.5.1 Deployment of Artificial Reefs (PMMSY scheme)

Artificial reefs are deployed to conserve

survival and increasing fish production. They

also discourage bottom trawling in nearshore

6.5.2. Sea Ranching

Declining marine fish stocks, particularly in

nearshore waters, necessitate scientific

interventions for resource enhancement and

long-term sustainability. Sea ranching is an

important resource conservation strategy

involving the release of hatchery produced

juveniles of commercially important marine

species into their natural habitat to replenish

depleted fish stocks.

The Department has already deployed

artificial reefs along the Tamil Nadu coast to

enhance marine biodiversity and create suitable

habitats for fish aggregation. Sea ranching of

economically important finfish and shellfish

species is being undertaken in these artificial

45

reef locations to improve stock enhancement

and maximise ecological benefits.

The programme will be expanded in a

phased manner across coastal districts through

stocking of commercially important candidate

species, in convergence with artificial reef

deployment and habitat restoration

programmes. The initiative is expected to

improve marine fish stock abundance, enhance

catch rates, strengthen ecosystem resilience and

directly benefit coastal fishers across the State.

6.6. Conservation of Sea Turtles

To protect endangered sea turtles and

their nesting habitats, installation of Turtle

Excluder Devices (TEDs) has been made

mandatory in trawl nets. Fishing is also

prohibited within 5 nautical miles of identified

nesting and breeding grounds from 1st January

to 30th April every year.

Fisheries, Forest Department and Costal Security

Group periodically reviews conservation

measures. Under PMMSY and State scheme for

the year 2025-26, a total of 2,663 TEDs have

been distributed and installed in trawl nets.

The White Paper on fiscal management of Tamil Nadu that was published in June 2026 sets the roadmap for better revenue mobilisation and administrative reforms, and has inter alia observed that the decline across major taxes like GST, VAT, and excise including revenues from mines and minerals has been mainly driven by administrative choices, leakages and corruption in the past rather than an underlying economic slowdown. It has also indicated that resolving this shortfall requires long-term, multi-year reforms focused on curbing corruption, enforcing compliance, and mobilizing resources efficiently. Some of the key factors highlighted in the White Paper are outlined below:

e Own-tax effort at a historic low — the SOTR-to-GSDP ratio fell to 5.45% in 2025-26, the lowest in two decades showing the sharpest decline among peer States in recent years.

e Large revenue foregone — decline in SOTR amounts to about Rs.1.23 lakh crore of annual revenue foregone, roughly 90% of the fiscal deficit in 2025-26.

e Unique to Tamil Nadu — Peer States like Maharashtra, and Karnataka have held on or have shown growth in SoTR-GSDP ratio, while Tamil Nadu alone has registered a steady decline.

e Broad-based weakness — the fall is reflected in all major taxes: GST, VAT on petroleum, State Excise, Stamp Duty and Motor Vehicle Tax.

e Cause is administrative, not structural — attributed to leakages, systemic corruption and administrative choices, primarily in commercial taxes, registration, excise and mining.

In the letter read above, the Project Director, Tamil Nadu Health Systems Project has stated that, the proposal was received from EMRI Green Health Services regarding the implementation of Mobile Service Vans (MSVs) to streamline the maintenance of the state's emergency ambulance fleet.

2. Tamil Nadu currently operates a fleet of 1,353 '108' ambulances, 130 JSSK vehicles, and 194 FHS project vehicles. However, the maintenance of this extensive fleet faces several critical hurdles:

The Original Equipment Manufacturer (Force Motors) has only 14 authorized service vendors across the state. Ambulances in districts without authorized vendors must travel long distances for minor repairs, leading to increased Nan-Case Kilometers (NCKM) and excessive fuel expenditure. Vehicles often remain off-road for more than a day for routine maintenance, significantly impacting emergency readiness.

3. The Project Director, Tamil Nadu Health Systems Project has further stated that:-

e The service provider proposes the pilot deployment of strategically located Mobile Service Vans and Mobile Service Bikes per region. These units will be equipped with essential diagnostic tools and spare parts to provide.

e On-site preventive maintenance at ambulance parking sites or

hospitals. . e Minor/medium repairs and immediate roadside breakdown assistance.

e In-house towing support to eliminate third-party charges. Cost Effectiveness and Financial Benefits:-

e The implementation is expected to be highly cost-effective, with projected savings arising from:

e Zero External Labour Costs: Utilizing in-house mobile technicians.

e Reduced Fuel Expenditure: Eliminating long-distance travel to workshops.

e Maximum Uptime: Aiming for near 100% fleet availability by reducing repair turnaround times.

4. Indicative pilot data for April 2026 suggests total monthly savings of approximately Rs.2,30,982/- across just three Mobile Service Vans (MSVs) units (TN20G1919, TN20G2298 and TN20G2144).

5. Considering the potential to optimize government assets and ensure uninterrupted emergency services to the public, the Project Director, Tamil Nadu Health Systems Project has requested the Government to consider and grant approval for this pilot initiative. The procurement, operation, and maintenance of the Mobile Service Vans will be entirely managed utilizing the regular, pre-approved operational budget of the 108 Ambulance Services.

1. Introduction

Our environment forms the basis of life on the

earth, upon which human health, economic

progress, and social well-being is closely linked

to it. It includes the air we breathe, the water we

use, the land we depend on, and the natural

systems that sustain life and development.

A clean and healthy environment is vital for

improving quality of life, supporting sustainable

growth, and preserving resources for future

generations.

65

In recent decades, rapid industrial growth,

urban expansion, rising resource consumption,

and changing climatic conditions have placed

exceptional pressure on environmental systems.

Pollution, waste generation, depletion of natural

resources, and climate change have become major

concerns that require urgent and continuous

attention. Addressing these issues demands

a balanced approach that combines environmental

protection with economic advancement and social

development.

Environmental protection is therefore a core

responsibility and an essential component of

sustainable development. It involves a broad range

of measures designed to prevent pollution,

conserve natural resources, reduce the effects of

climate change, promote efficient resource use,

and ensure compliance with environmental laws.

Through effective policy measures, regulatory

action, technological improvements, and public

build a cleaner, healthier, and more resilient future

for all.

the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board (TNPCB) in

1982 as a statutory body entrusted with

implementing environmental laws and regulations

in the State. The TNPCB functions under the

administrative control of the Department of

Environment, Climate Change, and Forest.

Secretary, 5 official members nominated by the
